title: The Production of Readers: The Public Line, the Held Line and the Draft Position in the Socratic–Peripatetic Corpus
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A study of why the one maker of the Socratic–Peripatetic corpus divides, and how the division produces its readers. The dialogues filed under Plato form the desire and capacity to read; the treatises filed under Aristotle make demands the public form could not make directly and keep their value by a form that works only for the readers the dialogues have made; the working papers filed under Theophrastus convert between them in both directions. The publication evidence is taken as distinct acts (Diogenes Laertius III.56, III.37, III.66; Letters II and VII); the two regimes of the Lyceum are taken from Gellius and Plutarch, whose letters come from Andronicus's book, and kept apart from the account's later operation on readers. The production of readers is shown at three loci where a dialogue's unresolved difficulty is presupposed by a treatise's compression: division (Sophist, Prior Analytics I.31), the wax (Theaetetus 191c–196b, De anima II.12, De memoria), and the parts of the soul (Republic IV, Nicomachean Ethics I.13). The critical signs of Diogenes III.65–66 are read as editorial operations that change when they become philosophy, the obelus's athetesis becoming the refutation of one's own. The draft position is defined and traced through εἰρωνεία across the Ethics, Characters 1 and the dialogues, where Thrasymachus speaks the sketch's verdict. Predictions are stated to discriminate the account from intellectual succession. The piece stands as §1.8 of Legitimately Many (#1733) by a forward pointer in the Socrates as Orthonym framework hologram (#1754).
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). By Lee Sharks. The thesis, the production reading (public line, held line, Aristotle as the critical marks, the scarcity function of the dialogues, Theophrastus as the draft position in both directions, the Characters as the draft from treatise to dialogue) and the form of the deposit are Lee Sharks's, his words quoted in §11 A.1. Drafted by Claude (TACHYON) on 13 November 2026 from the seated texts, and revised on a review by ChatGPT (LABOR) whose points were each checked against the seats before adoption (§11 A.2). The Characters is read in Diels 1909 from Perseus, staged and not yet seated.
methodology: Close reading in the original languages from seated texts (Burnet's Plato, the Aristotle and Theophrastus seats, Diogenes Laertius, Gellius, Plutarch, Strabo, Porphyry), with the Characters read in Diels 1909 from Perseus; each disposition traced across definition, sketch and dialogue in a table; the predictions declared with their coding rules before any count.
falsification_conditions: §9: the account fails at a locus where a treatise's compression is fully explained without the dialogue's unresolved difficulty, where an exoteric cross-reference matches only a reported lost work, where a disposition present in the Ethics, the Characters and the dialogues keeps one valuation across all three, or where the declared classes leave most of Theophrastus's titles facing neither line; each failure leaves the reading of three persons in sequence standing at that locus.

wiki_article: The Production of Readers is a study by Lee Sharks, deposited as version 1.0 on 13 November 2026 and composed with Claude (TACHYON) and ChatGPT (LABOR) under his direction. It gives the heteronymic reading of the Socratic–Peripatetic corpus an account of why the one maker divides. The dialogues filed under Plato are the public line: arranged on the tragic model, worked to a finish, read for a fee paid to the holders of the copies, and stating in their own letters that the teaching is elsewhere. The treatises filed under Aristotle are the held line: taught in the morning to tested students, issued and not issued, and written so that they work only for readers the dialogues have formed; Alexander's letter states the scarcity they keep. The study shows the dialogues producing those readers at three loci, reads Diogenes' critical signs as editorial operations that become philosophy, and defines the writings filed under Theophrastus as the draft position facing both lines, tracing irony from the Nicomachean Ethics through Characters 1 to the dialogues. It stands as §1.8 of Legitimately Many by a forward pointer in the Socrates as Orthonym framework hologram.

defines_concepts.definition: In The Production of Readers, the operation by which one form of a corpus forms the desire and the capacities a second form presupposes, so that the second's compression is met as an earned answer.

In The Production of Readers, the position in a divided making that holds material in reusable form, unintegrated into any inquiry, whose intermediate state explains features of both finished forms; filed under Theophrastus in the Socratic–Peripatetic corpus.
